holidays.name: National Tooth Fairy Day
holidays.description: Dig out the loose baby teeth and the spare change. This is the day to celebrate the tiny winged night-shift worker who swaps molars for money. Tuck a tooth under a pillow, write a note to the Tooth Fairy, or just feel good about the legend that makes losing a tooth less scary.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance with no single known founder. It celebrates the tradition of the Tooth Fairy, which grew popular in early 20th-century America. It built on older customs of rewarding children for lost teeth.
holidays.funFact: In many Spanish-speaking countries, the tooth-collecting hero is a mouse called Ratoncito Pérez, not a fairy.

holidays.name: National Take Your Cat to the Vet Day
holidays.description: Cat owners know the drill: the carrier comes out and the cat vanishes under the bed. This day nudges owners to book their feline's checkup, even if the cat plans to hold a grudge. Expect dramatic yowling in the car, and a healthier cat afterward.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, pet-awareness observance of unclear origin. It encourages regular veterinary visits for cats, who are often skipped because they hide illness so well.
holidays.funFact: Cats instinctively mask pain and illness, a survival trait from their wild ancestors. That is why routine checkups matter even when a cat seems perfectly fine.

holidays.name: Be an Angel Day
holidays.description: Time to earn your halo. This day invites you to do small, secret good deeds for others, like paying for a stranger's coffee, leaving a kind note, or helping a neighbor. Wings are optional, but kindness is not.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed among August's quirky days of celebration and promotes anonymous acts of kindness.
holidays.funFact: Studies on kindness suggest that doing small good deeds for others can lift your own mood too. Being an angel can be good for the angel as well.
